source_mapping.meaning: Opens the edit window through OpenEditWindow, applies the current map plane, then refreshes the edit and graph windows.
Gets object 4, computes columns=(right-left)/16 and rows=(bottom-top)/16+1, centers the map on the requested player point, clamps camera to plane extents, and clips map drawing to the edit viewport.
Uses the complete object identifier; call argument 4 while window 0 is current denotes object index 4 of window 0.
Switches MapPlane and centers/updates the edit view from the selected player-plane point.
Intersects the map viewport with the active window clip region; native rendering intersects this viewport with the caller's current clip.

viewport.rows_contract: The source adds one row after integer division. The final row is only painted inside the viewport clipping rectangle.

camera_contract.origin: focus - floor(visible cell count/2), then f_0250_0F2C clamp
camera_contract.live_scroll_note: Do not call resolve every frame after user scrolling; retain the live camera origin in the ongoing view state.

rendering.pixel_scope: Actual kind-9 resource bytes and source-derived 16x16 EGA layout are used. The output is a native indexed framebuffer. No physical EGA read-map or full DOS screen-pixel equality is claimed.
rendering.window_scope: This function draws map cells only. Window frame, labels, and other objects remain with the resource-backed window renderer; unsupported objects remain explicit errors.

generated_scene.source_plane_selection: session.world.current_ant_plane, equivalent to the SetDefaultWindows tail's SetMapPlane(MePlane)
generated_scene.resources: Actual SHARED sine table, HCEGANT tileset, and profile-0 window registry; no setup/resource callback is substituted.
generated_scene.observed: plane 2; player (36,11); camera (25,2); 418 cells; 3 cells with life

checks: Actual HCEGANT profile-0 window 0 is loaded and recalculated before resolution.
Viewport rect, 22x19 dimensions, player-centered camera, and edge clamps for planes 0, 2, and 3 are checked.
All logical cells of a full session NewGame scenario-1 world render with actual ground and nest resources.
Viewport clipping and narrower caller clipping preserve pixels outside the effective clip, then restore the original clip.
An unloaded or unrecalculated viewport window fails explicitly.
